# Sprint 1 - System Request

## System request

Name: Quick Phone Repair Management System

Project Sponsor: Ashiqullah Pardisi (ardisi1987@gmail.com)

Business Need: QuickPhone repairs phones, tablets, laptops, game consoles and other devices at two store locations. Its staff have no single, shared view of repair jobs and parts inventory. As a result, customers call to ask where their device is, repairs stall while waiting on parts that were not reordered in time, and devices risk being misplaced or released to the wrong person. This project aims to develop a system that schedules and tracks every repair from check-in through customer pickup and manages parts inventory levels. This gives staff and the owner better visibility into open repairs and inventory, allowing for better capacity and inventory planning.

Business Value: The system is estimated to return about 6 hours of staff time a week across both stores - roughly 315 hours a year, worth about $8,952 at estimated wage rates. A shared, current view of every job and automatic email alerts when a device is ready should cut "where's my device?" calls roughly in half, while linking parts inventory and purchase orders to repair jobs should halve the time technicians lose to stalled jobs and reduce inventory administration by about 40%. The 104 technician hours recovered each year are capacity for roughly 100 additional repairs — close to $12,000 in added annual revenue at an estimated $120 average repair, if demand supports it; this is the same hours valued as throughput rather than saved wages and is not additive to the figure above. Against this, cost is estimated at $1,550 one-time and $1,460 a year, giving an estimated three-year net present value of about $17,100 and payback in about two and a half months. All figures are preliminary estimates resting on assumed call and job volumes and on national wage rates, pending verification by owner. Beyond the financial case, tagging every device at check-in and verifying ticket, photo ID and signature at release targets zero lost or wrongly released devices per quarter, a full audit history of who checked in, quoted, repaired and released each device improves accountability, and one documented process at both stores shortens training and supports future growth.

Business Requirements: The system will let front desk staff check in a customer and device in one pass. This will collect information about customer, device, fault, condition and accessories create the repair job with a promised-by date, book drop-off appointments, assign a technician, and print a claim ticket and device tag label. Technicians will move jobs through defined statuses from check-in to pickup, record diagnoses, quotes and customer approvals, and reserve and consume parts, with jobs flagged automatically when awaiting parts; where a customer declines the quote, the job will be closed as not repaired and the device returned through the same release check as a completed repair. The manager will maintain a parts catalog with cost, supplier, device model and grade, see stock at each store, review an automatic low-stock list, record purchase orders and receive deliveries against them so stock and waiting jobs update together, transfer parts between the two stores, and correct stock for damaged, miscounted or returned parts so recorded quantities match the shelf. At pickup, staff will record the final cost and paid status and complete a required release check of ticket number, photo ID and signature. The system will email customers when their device is ready, keep a timestamped history of every status change, approval, part used, stock correction and release attributed to the staff member responsible, and give all staff and the owner one dashboard of open, overdue and awaiting-parts jobs and low stock across both stores. Access will be role-based for Front Desk, Technician, Manager and Owner, and the existing parts inventory will be imported at launch.

Special Issues/Constraints: System must be accessible from both stores and have the ability to print a device tag at check in. Customer information (contact details, signatures, etc) must be protected and encrypted in storage and in transit . Each staff member must authenticate to their own account so actions can be attributed.
